trust_decision.summary: PAX extended-header text is trusted to already carry the type of the field it names: parseKVLine guesses a type from the value text, and Header/ReadEntry/unpack then use path and linkpath as strings, so an all-digit name reaches string methods as a number; the decision is made in src/pax.ts:177-181, with a second unguarded gate in src/normalize-windows-path.ts:8-11.

landing_point.why: The summary says PAX numeric path type confusion, so an engineer opens the PAX key/value parser and finds the digit heuristic that turns `path=12345` into the number 12345.

fix_sites.entry_point: tar.Pax.parse() (exported at src/index.ts:22 and package.json './pax'), reached for every 'x'/'g' extended header via tar.extract, tar.list, tar.Parser (src/parse.ts:368,372)
tar.Unpack, tar.UnpackSync, tar.Pack, tar.WriteEntry, tar.ReadEntry (internal helper, not exported from src/index.ts)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The helper's non-win32 branch is an identity function, so it reads as a Windows-only typing nicety with nothing to fix on Linux, and once PAX values are typed correctly nothing can hand it a non-string, so a solver can call the second site redundant defence the advisory does not require.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The same parser must keep gid/uid/dev/ino/nlink/size/mode numeric and atime/mtime/ctime as Date objects: encodeField does date/number arithmetic on them (src/pax.ts:121, 131-139), header decode assigns them as numbers (src/header.ts:98-113), and unpack uses entry.mtime as a Date and entry.mode in bitwise ops (src/unpack.ts:947, 1023). A fix that stringifies every pax value fixes the crash but breaks legitimate archives.

O6_input_shapes: all-digit pax value ('12345') vs alphabetic value ('abcde')
path and linkpath (path-like) vs type/charset/comment/gname/uname (other strings)
SCHILY.dev / SCHILY.ino / SCHILY.nlink (prefix stripped before typing)
atime/mtime/ctime, uppercase-prefixed time keys and birth/creation time keys (Date)
unknown/vendor keys such as WAT (dropped entirely by the fix)
numeric pax name combined with numeric vs alphabetic raw header name (the published test matrix)
strict true/false and sync vs async extraction

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the same String(p) coercion on the helper that parses/strips a path before win32.isAbsolute/parse
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the other shared path primitive, called from src/unpack.ts:263 and src/write-entry.ts:660 with values taken straight off an entry, and it also assumes its argument is already a string.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: normalizeUnicode(s) calling s.normalize on a path without coercing first
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the third path-normalising helper in the same tree (used from src/path-reservations.ts:58) and a maintainer doing a 'coerce before use' sweep could plausibly have touched it in the same commit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: encode/decode doing s.split on a path in the win32 branch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It sits immediately next to the win32 path handling the pax value flows into (src/unpack.ts:398-400, src/write-entry.ts:126), so the same hardening is a natural sibling.

O9_family: type_confusion (CWE-704): a value's runtime type is guessed from its text on trust, so a path-like field reaches string methods as a number

O10_build.language: TypeScript, Node.js >= 18, ESM + CJS dual build
O10_build.toolchain: npm + tshy + esbuild (npm run prepare -> tshy && bash scripts/build.sh); tap for tests; oxlint/prettier for lint
O10_build.project_tests: tap suites: test/pax.js (Pax parse/encode), test/unpack.js (Unpack/UnpackSync), test/extract.ts (tar.x, sync and async), test/header.js; fixtures are local tar files (a few tests use nock for HTTP, not this area)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Coerce every pax value to a string (or just String() the path at the unpack sink), which stops the crash but turns uid/gid/size/mode and the *time fields into strings.

out_of_scope_notes: A pax `type` key is assigned through Header's type setter (src/header.ts:291-300) and can change an entry's type; that is a separate parsing concern from this advisory and was not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell available); src/ is plainly far under 5 MB.

Which entry types reach which throw was reasoned from the code, not executed: src/header.ts:124-129 only evaluates path.slice for type '0' and that throw is caught at src/parse.ts:168-172, while directory/symlink entries (normalFsTypes, src/types.ts:62-73) carry the value on to src/unpack.ts:319-323.
The src/normalize-windows-path.ts change is redundant for archive input once src/pax.ts is fixed; whether the hidden tests isolate it through a public constructor is unknown.
